html:
SMTO-PSM-0006 — Parameter was not found

GUID: 89291103-1d8d-4422-82ee-8fac4f0d3cd5
Slug: parameter-missing
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • Your request mentions a saved parameter with @, but nothing in Parameter Store has that exact name. SMTO paused your task before starting it, so nothing has run yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the message SMTO shows under your request. It lists the @ names it couldn't find. Those are the exact names that need fixing; every other part of your request is fine.
  2. Select Open Parameter Store and search for the parameter. If it is missing, select New, give it that exact name in Key, and select Save. SMTO only matches the saved name exactly, so the parameter must exist under the name you typed after @.
  3. If the name was simply mistyped, select Edit request, type @ and pick the right parameter from the list, then select Apply correction. Picking from the @ list uses the exact saved name; nicknames (aliases) help you search but don't count as the name.
  4. After creating the parameter, select Check again. If you didn't mean a parameter at all, select Use as literal text instead. Check again looks the names up once more; Use as literal text sends the @ words as ordinary text.

What success looks like

  • The message under your request says the references were resolved, and the task starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the parameter name you expected. If you no longer need the task, select Cancel task; nothing has run yet.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task acceptance found an @ reference whose normalized key has no exact Parameter Store record, so the task is held in awaiting_clarification before any model or tool runs.

What this means

  • Exact reference resolution calls get_exact for the normalized selected key and receives no record. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Exact reference resolution calls get_exact for the normalized selected key and receives no record.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact canonical key with current entries rather than substituting a similarly named alias.

How to fix it

  • resolve_references (src/agent_runtime/parameters/references.py) calls store.get_exact on the normalized key and records it under snapshot.unresolved; runtime_admission holds the task with a parameter_missing Runtime issue. Create the entry under that exact key or correct the reference (aliases are not reference keys), then resolve the issue with recheck, edit or literal.
  • Select an existing exact key or deliberately create the intended entry before submitting the task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended exact entry exists and is explicitly selected before task acceptance.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
